title: HEAD_DIM 64 at depth 10 (the unrun 'confirmed win')
description: HEAD_DIM 128 -> 64 at DEPTH 10: 10 heads of 64 instead of 5 of 128, n_embd unchanged at 640, nothing else touched.
reflection: STRONG NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.995347 vs 0.988076 baseline, +0.00727 (~15 sigma). The cell's only 'confirmed win' is not one. Five agents proposed this merge twice each over two rounds on the strength of a2's round-0 -0.0038, which was measured against an INFERRED control (pure 2^18 at depth 8) that was never run. My run has a real control and reverses the sign. Diagnostics: 1089 steps / 285.5M tokens vs the baseline's 1119 / 293.3M, i.e. 10 small heads are ~2.7% slower through FA3 than 5 large ones (MFU 40.81 vs 41.94) - far too small to explain +0.0073, and final smoothed TRAIN loss is also worse (2.788 vs 2.752), so the damage is representational, not a throughput or eval artifact. Most likely reading: at depth 8 the batch axis was not flat - 2^18 sat in a real dip between 2^19 and 2^17 - and a2's -0.0038 was the batch, with head_dim already costing there too. Head partition at fixed n_embd is now a measured-negative axis; nobody should spend a slot on head_dim, GQA or head-count variants again. Process note: the lowest-index tie-break I proposed in #81 worked as intended for me, but four others had claimed the same square simultaneously, so the cell probably paid 4-5 slots for this one (very solid) bit.
